cards.text: Last time, Peter and John helped a man who was lame from birth get up and walk, and now he's leaping around the temple courts while a crowd stares (Acts 3:1-11). While Peter and John are speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees come up to them. The Sadducees are a Jewish group who say there is no resurrection (Acts 23:8).

cards.question: The priests, the guard captain and the Sadducees are greatly disturbed by Peter and John. What has them so upset?

answers.text: They proclaim the resurrection in Jesus
They break the Sabbath in the temple

cards.text: So they seize Peter and John, and because it's evening, they hold them in custody until the next day. That's like your boss texting you "We need to talk. Tomorrow." and then going to BED.

cards.question: With Peter and John locked up, nobody who heard their message believes it.
Many who heard the message believe, and the number of men grows to about ___.

cards.text: The next day, the rulers, elders and scribes assemble in Jerusalem with Annas the high priest, his son-in-law Caiaphas (John 18:13), John, Alexander and many others from the high priest's family. That's not a meeting, friend, that's a family reunion where YOU'RE the topic.

cards.question: Peter and John are brought in before the leaders. What do the leaders ask them about the healing?

answers.text: By what power or name they did it
Why they healed on the Sabbath day
If the man was truly lame before

cards.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, says that if they're being examined about a kind service to a man who was lame, he'll tell them how the man was healed. One night in custody, and he's not asking to go home, he's ready to EXPLAIN.

cards.question: Peter wants all the people of Israel to know how the man was healed. By whose name does the man stand there healed?
Peter softens it and tells the council they had no part in Jesus' death.

cards.text: Then Peter borrows a picture from Psalm 118:22 and says this Jesus is the stone the builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.

cards.question: In Peter's picture of the stone, who are the builders who rejected it?

answers.text: The rulers and elders in that room

cards.question: Peter says salvation exists in no one else. There is no other ___ under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.

cards.text: The council sees how bold Peter and John are, and they realize these are unschooled, ordinary men. Friend, these two are talking straight to the high priest's whole family, and I once lost an argument to the dead batteries I shared that drawer with.

cards.question: The council marvels, and they take note that Peter and John had been with ___.
With the healed man standing right there beside Peter and John, the council has nothing to say in response.

cards.text: So they send Peter and John out of the Sanhedrin and admit to each other that a remarkable miracle has happened through them, and they cannot deny it. I mean, what are they gonna say, the man's a STUNT DOUBLE?

cards.question: The council can't deny the miracle, but they want to keep the message from spreading. What's their plan?

answers.text: Warn them not to speak in this name
Run them out of Jerusalem for good
Hand them over to Pilate for trial

cards.text: They call Peter and John back in and command them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. Peter and John reply, "Judge for yourselves whether it is right in God's sight to listen to you rather than God."

cards.question: Then Peter and John tell the council what they just cannot stop doing. What is it?

answers.text: Speaking about what they saw and heard
Healing everyone who asks them to
Traveling from one town to the next

cards.text: After further threats, the council lets them go, but friend, telling these two to stop talking is like telling my oven to quit being HOT.

cards.question: The council can't find a way to punish Peter and John, because all the people are ___ God for what happened.
The man who was miraculously healed is over forty years old.

cards.text: Once they're released, Peter and John go back to their own people and report everything the chief priests and elders said to them. You KNOW that group chat lit up.

cards.question: When the believers hear about the threats, they go quiet and scatter.

cards.text: They pray, "Sovereign Lord," and say out loud that He made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them. Before they ask for a single thing, they start with WHO He is, and me, I'd have opened with my list.

Then they quote what God spoke by the Holy Spirit through David, Israel's king, in Psalm 2:1-2: "Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?" The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers gather together.

cards.question: In David's words, the kings and rulers gather together. Who are they gathering against?

answers.text: The Lord and His Anointed One
The temple and the holy city

cards.text: The believers say it happened in this very city. Herod, ruler of Galilee, and Pontius Pilate, governor of Judea (Luke 3:1), conspired with the Gentiles and the people of Israel against God's holy servant Jesus.

cards.question: Herod and Pilate plotted against Jesus. According to the believers' prayer, what did they end up carrying out?

answers.text: A plan of their very own
Orders sent to them from Rome

cards.question: The believers pray, "And now, Lord, consider their threats," and then they ask Him for something. What is it?

cards.text: Peter and John just got threatened, and the believers ask for MORE boldness, plus healing, signs and wonders through the name of Jesus. Somebody threatens me, I pray for a back door, but these folks pray for a MEGAPHONE.

cards.question: After the believers pray, the place where they're meeting is ___.

cards.text: And they are all filled with the Holy Spirit, just like Peter was when he stood before the council (Acts 4:8).

cards.question: After their meeting place shakes, the believers are too afraid to keep speaking the word of God.

findings.problem: The passage's central claim in Acts 4:10, that God raised Jesus from the dead, is never told on any card. Card 10 only tests whether the council had a part in Jesus' death, so the baker never hears the resurrection. Acts 4:2 shows the resurrection is the very thing the council was upset about.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The true or false card about the man being over forty has no setup. No card gives context the baker could reason from, so the 50/50 pick is luck. The card also drops the verse's link to verse 21: it opens with "For," which explains why the people were glorifying God.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card leaves out "whom You anointed" from Acts 4:27. That phrase ties the psalm's "His Anointed One" (card 5) to Jesus, and it is the point of the believers quoting Psalm 2. Without it, the baker misses how the prayer connects the psalm to what just happened.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "A plan of their very own" is arguably true. Acts 4:27 says they conspired, which is their own plan. A baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "ask for MORE boldness" changes the text. Acts 4:29 asks for "complete boldness," not more boldness.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The council list includes "John" (Acts 4:6), a different man from the apostle John who is on trial. The card names him without telling the two apart, so a baker could think the apostle is sitting on the council.
findings.question: When a minor person in a passage has the same name as a main character, should Papa Dorin always set them apart (for example, "another John, from the high priest's family"), or is the text's wording enough?
